Against the morning snapshot of 79,910.1 price is DOWN 142.5 points (-0.18 percent), but that flat-looking delta hides the whole story of the half-session: price first extended to 80,008.2 at 12:55 UTC, then broke hard to 79,199.0 at 14:32 UTC - an 809.2-point flush, the largest single move of the day - and has since bought back 568.6 points of it.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 79,490.0. That is 277.6 points under spot and it sits 118.9 points - roughly half an hourly ATR on the 240.21 reading - BENEATH the 79,608.9 low of the 16:00 UTC hourly candle, which is the newest higher low of the recovery off 79,199.0. I apply the half-ATR-beyond-a-proven-wick rule to the MOST RECENT proven wick on each side rather than the session extreme, because after a mid-session flush the tighter pair is the informative one. A settled close under 79,490 would mean the ascending sequence 79,199.0 to 79,382.4 to 79,608.9 has broken and the flush low is being re-approached with the 79,250 long bucket already spent underneath it.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 79,915.0. That is 147.4 points over spot and 119.5 points - half an hourly ATR - ABOVE the 79,795.5 high of the 16:00 UTC hourly candle, the level that has already capped this recovery once. It also clears the 1H EMA20 at 79,819.0 and the EMA50 at 79,773.3 in the same move, so a settled close there is the first thing that would say the flush was a liquidity grab inside an uptrend rather than the start of a lower-high structure.

decisionBox.changed: Position stays ADD for a third consecutive session, but this is the first time it is being held THROUGH a gate that fired against it. Morning's reduce level of 79,650.0 triggered at the 14:00 UTC hourly close of 79,543.7 - the gate did its job and the breakdown was real. What changed between then and now is that the market immediately un-did it: 79,199.0 was bought within two hourly candles, price closed back above the 4H EMA20 at 79,647.8, and the flush turned out to be almost entirely forced long liquidation (1,042,315 USD long against 33,915 USD short in the window, a 30-to-1 split). Open interest is down 57.5m (-2.65 percent) on morning and the OKX 1H account ratio has fallen 1.11 to 1.05, the least crowded long book of this series. Both gates move DOWN with the structure: reduce from 79,650.0 to 79,490.0, add from 80,135.0 to 79,915.0. The add here is the smallest of the three because cash is nearly exhausted, not because conviction rose.

liquidation.note: 653,398 USD across 52 fills, 652,627 of it LONG against 772 short. This is the single largest cluster in the whole 10.4-hour window and it is the bucket that did the damage: the 14:32 UTC flush to 79,199.0 ran straight through it. Magnet stays TRUE not because it can pull price again from here - it has already fired - but because a cluster this one-sided defines where the forced sellers were, and price now sits 267.6 points above it with nothing between. If the 79,490 reduce gate settles, this is the shelf the market re-tests.

264,436 USD across 12 fills, 241,721 of it LONG. This bucket is effectively AT spot - the centre is 79,750 and price is 79,767.6, 17.6 points away - and it is where the first wave of longs was taken out on the way down before the deeper 79,500 flush. It is stale as a magnet for exactly that reason: the positions are gone. Its value is as a reference point, showing the breakdown began right here rather than at the session high.

147,959 USD across 28 fills, 100 percent LONG, zero short. This is the tail of the flush - the last longs out, right at the 79,199.0 low. 28 fills for only 148k USD means these were small, scattered positions rather than size, which is the signature of a wick bottom rather than a distribution zone. Magnet FALSE: it has been fully cleared and there is no crowd left there to squeeze.

10,436 USD across 8 fills, almost all SHORT. The collapse of this bucket is the cleanest read in the report. At the midnight snapshot it held 1,191,230 USD, at morning 1,141,825 USD, and it is now 10,436 USD - a 99 percent decay as old fills rolled out of the 100-fill window with essentially nothing replacing them. The overhead short cluster that has capped this range for three sessions is now genuinely spent. That removes the fuel for a squeeze through 80,000, but it also removes the sellers.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is DOWN, a change from morning's BALANCED, and the reason is flow rather than structure. Liquidation flow in this window is 1,042,315 USD long against 33,915 USD short - 30.7 to 1, the most lopsided reading recorded in this series - which says every bit of forced activity has been sellers being taken out, not buyers. Funding has flipped back positive to +0.00284 percent from essentially zero at morning, so the longs who remain are paying again. Open interest is 2,109,775,512 USD, DOWN 57.46m (-2.65 percent) on morning: leverage genuinely left the market rather than rotating. The counterweight, and the reason bias is still range-with-a-bullish-tilt rather than bearish, is that the account ratio fell to 1.05 - the crowded-long condition that made the downside pull dangerous has itself been resolved by the flush.

calibration.rollingRecord: Settled-close gates: 22 correct out of the last 23 evaluated sessions. Morning's reduce gate at 79,650.0 FIRED and fired correctly - the 14:00 UTC hourly candle settled at 79,543.7, 106.3 points below the level, and price went on to print 79,199.0 within the same hour. That is the first reduce trigger in eight sessions and it caught a genuine 809.2-point break, so the half-ATR-beyond-a-proven-wick spacing is validated rather than undermined. The add gate at 80,135.0 was never threatened; the highest settled hourly close since the morning snapshot was 79,930.0 at 12:00 UTC, 205 points short.
calibration.note: Acting did NOT help this time and the report should say so plainly. Morning added a 5 USDT spot tranche at 79,910.1; spot is 79,767.6, so that tranche is down 0.18 percent and the wallet took the full flush on a book that was already 96 percent invested. The reasoning was sound and the outcome was bad - a distinction worth keeping. What the gate proved is that the discipline layer works even when the discretionary layer is wrong: had the reduce been executed on the 14:00 close at 79,543.7, it would have sold 224 points below where price is now, so firing the gate would ALSO have hurt. Two sessions in a row of small-loss adds, one correct gate that would have been a bad fill, and a market that keeps resolving inside 79,200-80,200.
